lead_headline: Restaurant pipeline swells to 35 active leads as 7 new detections land—Fusion by Tinos Kitchen and Taqueria Los Gallitos hit Wynkoop and Globeville while foreclosure filings plunge 33% week-over-week

restaurant.blurb: 7 new leads today push the active roster to 35 total (17 openings, 18 closures/temp closures). Fresh openings: Fusion by Tinos Kitchen preps Wynkoop Street debut from Englewood's successful Tino's Kitchen operators, Taqueria Los Gallitos replaces defunct Taco John's in Globeville, C Burger (regenerative beef smashburger) launches at Union Station's McGregor Square. Closure trail: Colfax and Cream confirms shuttered at Capitol Hill Broadway location (December closure, detected today), joins Pearl Street sibling in the morgue. California Pizza Kitchen Cherry Creek resurfaces as summer 2025 casualty after 25-year run. Week's tally now stands at 2 confirmed openings versus 5 closures—churn accelerating as Q1 ends.

foreclosure.blurb: 33 new filings this week marks a 33% drop from last week's 49, extending the post-winter deceleration into its third consecutive week. Total exposure: $11.1M, with Douglas County's $628K Lumos Lane property topping the roster. 63 auctions scheduled next seven days. Weld County still leads active cases at 345, El Paso follows at 375. Zero filings breached the $2M threshold this week—first time since tracker launch. Three-week slide from 49→33 suggests spring's traditional auction heat may arrive late or muted this cycle.

reputation.blurb: 8 mentions yesterday lift the 7-day total to 53 across 15 unique sources—a 960% surge from prior week's 5, marking the tracker's first full apples-to-apples comparison since launch. Denver Post dominates with 22 citations, Instagram contributes 8, Facebook and Hoodline each add 4-5. Notable Tuesday pickups: hotel foreclosure coverage, My Brother's Bar owner's gift card platform launch, Littleton industrial sale above $20M. Google News RSS captures 52 of 53 total mentions—social discovery remains marginal. Week-over-week explosion from 5→53 suggests either tracker maturation or genuine earned media acceleration; next seven days will clarify baseline velocity.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +3 yesterday (5 new, 2 canceled) recovers Monday's −1 stumble and edges MTD to +11 (+1.0/day), with 90-day cumulative at +76. Past two weeks reveal sustained churn volatility: catastrophic −4 on March 5 followed by three-day +8 rally (March 6-9), then Monday's single-cancellation hiccup before Tuesday's modest rebound. The 7-day net of +6 trails prior week's +11, signaling deceleration despite Tuesday's positive tick. YTD pace holds at +1.2/day—still outpacing March's 1.0 rate, but the weekly slowdown and persistent high-cancellation days (7 cancels March 5, 6 on March 4) suggest acquisition momentum cooling while churn stabilizes at elevated baseline.
